Sean/Tessa/Karthik —

Quick read of ACME's redlines and suggested path forward:

1) Term length: Commercially acceptable to do 36 months. Recommend adding a defined price escalation schedule tied to committed volume tiers (e.g., +3% year 2, +3% year 3) rather than open negotiation language. That keeps predictability for both sides.

2) Data residency carveout: we can support EU-only processing for a subset of workloads via an Exhibit-level carveout that enumerates the dataset IDs / API endpoints subject to EU processing. This avoids changing core MSA processing definitions. Include a mutual certification process and a statement that additional infrastructure costs are charged as an Addendum.

3) Capacity/Order Form: Accept conversion of burst -> committed if Finance signs off. Require a minimum 60-day lead time for on-prem routing changes and include a clause about burst overage billing at a defined rate.

4) Termination for convenience: propose pro-rated credits for unused committed term calculated on remaining months at the then-current committed rate less any usage fees; cap liability to 6 months of committed fees. Do not accept an immediate refund model.

5) Timing: Legal can turn around a marked MSA and an updated Order Form + Exhibit B by end of day Thursday (7/13) if sales can confirm target pricing tiers today.

I'll draft suggested redline snippets for Section 5.2 (Data Processing), Section 9 (Termination & Credits), and Exhibit B (Capacity Schedule).

-Laura
